answer: Because the timing is written down against the ivory challenge, the onyx audit can replay the wharf history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 79 submissions and hold every participant open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 9 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
